messages.subject: Re: How to hide sidebar when using a beamer to let maximum visibility to outputs ?
messages.subject_clean: How to hide sidebar when using a beamer to let maximum visibility to outputs ?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Guys,

I finally succeed. Here is how.
Code is here : https://github.com/uclouvain-selt/shiny/tree/master/simpleic
Result is here : http://sites.uclouvain.be/selt/shiny/simpleic/

First, i have put a checkbox in the main panel. The label is "Full screen".
When this checkbox is checked, all the sidebarpanel is hidden with the Laurent's technique :  a conditionalPanel arround all the sidebar panel.

But doing this, the span8 div is not resized, it is still 62,812%width, so i resized it with Jquery to a width of 95% as Jquery is already loaded with shiny. I put a script.js file in www/js and in this file i change CSS of several elements to allow me to use the maximum place for the app : https://github.com/uclouvain-selt/shiny/blob/master/simpleic/www/js/scripts.js

Along this, i set some display sets of options for my plots to be sure that everything is not too small when beeing with a beamer. I have set two displays : 800x600 and 1024x768. The parameters are set in server.R and update the cex of all elements, the width and height of each plots, the margins,etc.

These 3 steps 1) conditionalPanel arround sidebarPanel, driven by a checkbox in mainPanel, 2) CSS driven by this checkbox using Jquery, 3) display setting drivent by a select in ui.R, have allowed me to reach my goal : we now can use this app during lectures using a beamer and maximise space to be seen by students.

The last challenge is when you have several tabPanel, you have to duplicate all the inputs you put in each tabs, like, for exemple actionButtons.If you do not duplicate them, all whith an unique ID, all the stuff is freezing because you can not have duplicate inputs with same ids. But this is only if you have several tabs. I will post an exemple later when this part will be finished.

Thanks to all for advises and suggestions that drove me to the solution.

Grégoire

messages.body_plain:
I am not sure what you are after but I think this should give you a good start.

#-server.R

smpl<-read.csv("smpl.csv")

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$smplTab<-renderDataTable({
    smpl[c(input$cname1, input$cname2)]
  }, options = list(aLengthMenu = c(5, 30, 50), iDisplayLength = 5))

  output$myplot<-renderPlot({
    plot(smpl[c(input$cname1, input$cname2)])
  })

})

#-ui.R

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Road Accident Analysis")
  ,sidebarPanel(
      selectInput(inputId="cname1",choices=names(smpl),label="Variable1")
      ,selectInput(inputId="cname2",choices=names(smpl),label="Variable2")
      )
  ,mainPanel(
    dataTableOutput("smplTab")
    ,plotOutput("myplot")
    )
  )
)

I like the first option. In the second, you'll need to watch out for an unchanged library path -- i.e. you may be running the R process as root but still inherit in your R library settings from your unprivileged user, thus you'll just end up installing into the same library you would have without being root.

However, you can use the '-i' option on Linux to request that you get the full-fledged root session which gets around this problem:

Again, the cleanest is probably Tyler's first solution.

Hi,

First: congrats on 0.9! This shiny/ggvis/knitr ecosystem is really turning into something amazing!

Second: I might be trying to use ggvis and shiny in a way that "hasn't been built yet".

If that's the case, a perfectly acceptable answer will be, "Not yet, wait until we have built it".

Here are the nuggets of what I am trying to do - the full shiny app is at https://gist.github.com/ijlyttle/9954598/99dbf4ae1084f9cc3468cd299216ccb3f223dba0 :

This works interactively and in shiny:

    ggvis(diamonds, props(x = ~table)) +
      layer_histogram(binwidth = 1)

This works interactively but not in shiny:

    ggvis(diamonds,
          by_group(cut),
          props(x = ~table, fill = ~cut),
          transform_bin(binwidth = 1)) +
    layer(
      props(x = ~xmin__, x2 = ~xmax__, y = ~count__, fillOpacity := 0.6),
      layer(
        transform_stack(),
        mark_rect(props(y = ~ymax__, y2 = ~ymin__))
      )
    )

I suspect this has to do with non-standard evaluation not playing well with reactivity.

Can you guys shed any light on this?

(I'm guessing shiny is the place to post this, but I am happy to move it to ggvis if that's the thing to do.)

Side issue: could the runGist() function take a second argument based on the revision hash of a gist, in support of reproducibility?

Ian

Great! You're halfway there.

The other piece of the puzzle is the "hosting mode <http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#hosting-model>." Bu default, you're using site_dir which hosts a whole directory of applications. What you want is app_dir, which hosts a single application.

So you could use app_dir mode by doing something like:

location / {
   ...
   app_dir /srv/shiny-server/myapp;
}

That would host an individual application at the base URL.

Jeff

messages.subject_clean: popups don't work anymore with shiny 0.9.1
messages.body_plain:
Hello Stéphane,
You may want to try this code with Shiny 0.9.1. I have tested it with your example and it works well on my side.

Here is the helpPopup function, with some improvements:

# popup function (from J. Cheng, Shiny-discuss, 2/7/13)
# C Boivin:  add a parameter "glue" to label the button
# or to place an object on (button, selectInput, slider)

helpPopup <- function(title, content,
              placement=c('right', 'top', 'left', 'bottom'),

              trigger=c('click', 'hover', 'focus', 'manual'),
              glue = NULL) {

  tagList(
    singleton(
      tags$head(
           tags$script("$(function() { $(\"[data-toggle='popover']\").popover(); })")
      )
    ),

    tags$a(
    #  href = "#", class = "tip", `data-toggle` = "popover",
      href = "#",
      class = "btn btn-default",
      `data-toggle` = "popover",

      title = title,
      `data-content` = content,

      # added this parameter
      `data-html` = TRUE,
      #

      `data-animation` = TRUE,
      `data-placement` = match.arg(placement, several.ok=TRUE)[1],
      `data-trigger` = match.arg(trigger, several.ok=TRUE)[1],

       glue,
      tags$i(class="icon-info-sign")
    ),
    # CB added for popup width control
    tags$style(type='text/css', ".popover { width: 400px; relative; left: 320px !important; }")
    # end add
  )
}

ui code:
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Popup examples"),
  sidebarPanel(
    wellPanel(
    # first example

      helpPopup("Import a data file",

      includeMarkdown("www/helpPopups/help_upload.Rmd"),
    #  you may also use: includeHTML("your-file.html"),
    #  you may also  link your html file with a .css stylesheet
      placement='right',
      trigger='click',
      glue = " click on popup"
      )
    ),
   wellPanel(
      # second example
      helpPopup("Glue the help on something",
      includeMarkdown("www/helpPopups/help_upload.Rmd"),
     placement='right',
     trigger='hover',
     glue =  selectInput("sel1", "",
        choices = c("first choice, a long text to enlarge this box",
                   "second choice",
                    "third choice"),
       selected = "first choice")
     # you may also glue the help on a button: glue = actionButton()
    )
    )
  ),
  mainPanel(
  )
))

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: spark vs glimmer vs ShinyApps.io
messages.subject_clean: spark vs glimmer vs ShinyApps.io
messages.body_plain:
Glimmer and Spark have the same configuration (Glimmer came first and when we ran out of room on that server we set up Spark). We set them up when Shiny was brand new so that users could try deploying apps without having to set up their own Linux machines. However, they aren't a sustainable long-term solution. We're no longer creating new accounts on Glimmer and Spark. These servers will go away "someday" but we don't currently know when that will be.

ShinyApps.io is, as you say, a platform as a service. We intend to turn this into a commercial service with free and paid tiers. That said, it is still in alpha stage and has some maturing to do.

Specific differences:
Glimmer and Spark have a built-in RStudio Server instance. ShinyApps.io does not.
Glimmer and Spark require you to use rsync, scp, sftp, or RStudio Server to upload your applications. ShinyApps.io has a convenient "shinyapps" package on CRAN that lets you upload and deploy with one R command.
Glimmer and Spark are running R 2.15 and we don't have a way to upgrade them to R 3.0 without breaking everyone's applications. ShinyApps.io is running R 3.0 and won't have a problem with upgrades in the future.
All applications on Glimmer and Spark are accessible to anyone who knows the URL. ShinyApps.io applications can require username/passwords (this will eventually be a paid feature).
Glimmer and Spark have a persistent hard drive; storage on ShinyApps.io is ephemeral. (We hope to improve this on ShinyApps in the future.)
Security is much better on ShinyApps.io due to greater isolation between different users/apps.

messages.subject: Re: How to conditionally append a list using action buttons
messages.subject_clean: How to conditionally append a list using action buttons
messages.body_plain:
In your server function (note, I haven't tested this code but it seems like it should work):

values <- reactiveValues(answers = logical(0))
observe({
  if (input$yes == 0) return()
  isolate({
    values$answers <- c(values$answers, TRUE)
  })
})
observe({
  if (input$no == 0)
    return()
  isolate({
    values$answers <- c(values$answers, FALSE)
  })
})

Then refer to values$answers wherever you want to get at the answers. (Unlike with a reactive expression, you don't need to do values$answers(), just values$answers will do--like an input.)

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am new to the group and trying to learn a lot about R and Shiny. (I am quite new to this, just about 1~2 weeks)
As I am learning along, I am doing my own project, trying to write a Shiny tutorial for my fellow colleagues.
I have done farily extensive amount of work on this project, but just came down to a huge obstacle.

My problem is that, I do not know how to incorporate Shiny application into a HTML file, which was generated by R Markdown file + Knitr.

For tutorials purpose, I have been using Code Chunks + screenshot,

```{r shiny hello example, eval=FALSE}
  library(shiny)
  runExample("01_hello")
```
with a screenshot of "01_hello"

This is fairly straightforward and easy to read as a tutorial, but I was wondering if I can do something like what http://shiny.rstudio.com website does.

For example, I would be writing my guides/explanations about Shiny here
Then the Shiny application with ui.R and server.R <- important!!

If I use iframe, it doesn't seem to work the same way as RunApp does in R Console. It will just show the application itself.

Do you guys have any suggestion?

-- quoted from a previous topic --
You can use an iframe -- that's actually what's done on the main RStudio Shiny page: http://www.rstudio.com/shiny/

The code there is something like this:
<iframe src="http://glimmer.rstudio.com/rstudio/faithful/" style="border: none; width: 440px; height: 500px"></iframe>

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: accessing server data on shinyapps
messages.subject_clean: accessing server data on shinyapps
messages.body_plain:
Hi Patrick,

Good news/bad news here. The bad news is, this specific task will be a bit more difficult in ShinyApps in the short-term. The good news is that once you take the hit of refactoring your code, your apps will be much more scalable and reliable.

ShinyApps is designed using the new model for how servers should be organized (here's one  <https://blog.engineyard.com/2014/pets-vs-cattle>good explanation), but the central tenant is: never trust hardware. No server should be expected to run eternally, no single hard drive should be expected to run without failure, etc. So we built ShinyApps around the model that if any device ever starts acting up, we can shoot it and have minimal consequences. The good news is that this will make the service much more reliable in the long-run, as we won't have to manually move your applications off of a server if the memory goes bad, rather we'll just instantly spin your apps up in a better machine.

But unfortunately, that means that you can't trust that your application will always be running on a machine with access to the same hard drives. We will eventually want to come up with ways for you to centrally store data reliably in ShinyApps, but that feature isn't there just yet. So that means that you shouldn't expect files you write to disk in ShinyApps to be there eternally. The documentation discusses this briefly <https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps/blob/master/guide/guide.md#application-instances>.

(One caveat for on-disk data is data that you bundle into your application at the outset when you deploy it. We make sure that static data is available to your application wherever it's running. So we're just talking about data that your application creates dynamically.)

So how do you write data out of a Shiny application? I usually recommend Amazon's S3 service <http://aws.amazon.com/s3/?sc_channel=PS&sc_campaign=AWS_Free_Tier_2013&sc_country=US&sc_publisher=Google&sc_medium=Brand_Core_AWS_S3_E&sc_content=36369200322&sc_detail=Aws%20s3&sc_category=storage_CDN&sc_segment=s3&sc_matchtype=e>. There are R packages that help you read/write data here (like this one <http://www.inside-r.org/packages/cran/AWS.tools/docs/s3.mb>). The basic idea is that you would read the data in from S3 when your application starts up, then write it out periodically as you change it.

Sorry this isn't yet well-documented. We'll be sure to add this to the Todo list; I think an example or two in this area would be helpful.

Let me know if you have any trouble with it.

Jeff

messages.body_plain:
Hi folks -

A Shiny app of mine is getting ready to go 'live' to several users.  I'm trying to understand what kind of traffic a Shiny server (not pro server) can handle,
and how to best manage it.  One question I have is, what exactly happens if, say, a session is started by a user and the user decides to abort the session
by closing the browser window, while Shiny is busy making a long calculation?  I assume the server 'figures it out' and releases any resources used by that
session, but that's just my assumption... do I need to be concerned about making sure my app cleans up after itself?

Related to that, since my app involves some relatively long calculations, I can anticipate my users thinking 'oh never mind, it's taking too long' and having a desire
for a ;'reset' button (vs having to start a whole new session).  In fact I have been asked for this feature.  Is there any simple way to build in that kind of capability in a Shiny app?

thank you.

messages.body_plain:
I agree this would be a useful example to add to our gallery. I'll see what we can whip up.

I understand your hesitation with S3, but I will say it's one of the safer pay-as-you-go services I've worked with. I, too, have made my share of gaffes, but accidentally uploading hundreds of GB of data to S3 would be quite a feat! For the amount of data you're dealing with, I'd be surprised if you were able to muster up an S3 bill over $10, even with a heinous bug.

The being said, if you wanted to send to FTP, it sounds like that's something RCurl can handle, though I've never done it in R myself. http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3620426/how-to-upload-a-file-to-a-server-via-ftp-using-r.

I don't have a full-fledged example for you, but the basic idea would be to read out the file from S3/FTP when Shiny starts, then write it back to update the file whenever you make a change (complete a survey). As long as you only run one instance of this process at a time, you won't have to worry about conflicts or processes overwriting each-other's data.

I'll be sure to post back if/when we're able to get an example together.

Jeff

messages.body_plain:
Chandler,

In recent versions of Shiny Server, the working directory is set to be the same as the dir in which the application is housed.

Shiny needs to be installed for the user running the application, which is often the `shiny` user (see documentation for the run_as setting in the docs). I'd recommend logging in as that user (`sudo -i ; su shiny`), opening R, and trying to `library(shiny)`. You'll need to make sure that command can execute properly before Shiny Server will be able to start Shiny processes for you.

Jeff

messages.body_plain:
Thanks to all for this thread!

Like Stephane, I need to make my version of file "about_formulas.Rmd" dynamic. Towards this goal, I added the argument "input" to function "includeRmd", so that I can use \Sexpr{input$[my object]} within "about_formulas.Rmd". For example, I could write
$ \Sexpr{input$x^2} $
I was pleasantly surprised with the fact that the dollar symbol before "x" does not get confused with the delimiter symbols. On the other hand, mathjax only loads the first resulting file, not to following ones. That is, as soon as I change input$x, I lose the mathjax rendering. Any ideas? Here are sample files:

### ui.R  ###

require(shiny)
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  headerPanel('Testing'),

  sidebarLayout(
      sidebarPanel( sliderInput("x", "Value of x", min = 0, max = 1, value = 0.5) ),
      mainPanel( uiOutput("myhelp"), textOutput("text") )
  )
))

### server.R  ###

library(shiny)
source('./includeRmd.R')
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$myhelp <- renderUI({ list(
    includeRmd("about_formulas.Rmd",input),

    tags$script(src = 'https://c328740.ssl.cf1.rackcdn.com/mathjax/2.0-latest/MathJax.js?config=TeX-AMS-MML_HTMLorMML', type = 'text/javascript')

  )})

  output$text <- renderText({
            paste("Current value of x:", input$x)
        })
})

## includeRmd.R ###

includeRmd <- function(path, input=NULL){

    if (!require(knitr)) stop("knitr package is not installed")
    if (!require(markdown)) stop("Markdown package is not installed")
    shiny:::dependsOnFile(path)
    contents = paste(readLines(path, warn = FALSE), collapse = '\n')

    html <- knitr::knit2html(text = contents, fragment.only = TRUE,

            encoding='UTF-8',
            options=c("use_xhtml", "smartypants", "base64_images", "mathjax", "highlight_code"),
            header=HTML("<script type='text/x-mathjax-config'>
                            MathJax.Hub.Config({
                            tex2jax: {
                            inlineMath: [ ['$','$'], ['\\(','\\)'] ],
                            processEscapes: true
                            }
                            });
                            </script>"),
            extensions=c("no_intra_emphasis", "tables", "fenced_code", "autolink", "strikethrough",
                    "lax_spacing", "space_headers", "latex_math")
    )

    return(HTML(html))
}

## about_formulas.Rmd ###

Squared value of x: $x^2 = \Sexpr{input$x^2}.$

New versions of Shiny (>=0.9) offer input selection via selectize.js <http://brianreavis.github.io/selectize.js/> .

Selectize.js offers additional functionality based on Plugins e.g. "remove_button" or "drag_drop", see also here  <https://github.com/brianreavis/selectize.js/tree/master/src/plugins>.

Is it possible to use this functionality? ( I use Shiny 0.9.1)

selectizeInput( ..... ,  options = I("plugins: ['remove_button']") )

If possible, what is the correct way of using these features?

kind regards, Herman

messages.subject: Re: using selectize.js plugin options in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: using selectize.js plugin options in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

The options argument should be a list, and I("plugins:
['remove_button']") is a character string. Please try the minimal
example below:

library(shiny)
runApp(list(
  ui = fluidPage(
    selectizeInput(
      'foo', 'FOO', LETTERS, multiple = TRUE, options = list(plugins =
list('remove_button'))
    )
  ),
  server = function(input, output) {}
))

If you want more plugins, just add their names to the list(), e.g.
list('remove_button', 'restore_on_backspace')

Regards,
Yihui

Op woensdag 16 april 2014 18:22:26 UTC+2 schreef Yihui Xie:

> Hi,
>
> The options argument should be a list, and I("plugins:
> ['remove_button']") is a character string. Please try the minimal
> example below:
>
> library(shiny)
> runApp(list(
>   ui = fluidPage(
>     selectizeInput(
>       'foo', 'FOO', LETTERS, multiple = TRUE, options = list(plugins =
> list('remove_button'))
>     )
>   ),
>   server = function(input, output) {}
> ))
>
> If you want more plugins, just add their names to the list(), e.g.
> list('remove_button', 'restore_on_backspace')
>
> Regards,
> Yihui
>

You could look at including that code in global.R if you also are using it on your server. But I'd bet that some code in there is causing the problem (missing library? typo?) Jeff

James and ZJ: First, thanks to both of you for your contributions. Please, consider the following: th2 = HTML('
  • a
  • b
    • b1
    • b2
  • c
') When th2 is placed in a jstree, the node "b" is automatically "opened" due to the class=jstree-open designation. In addition, this node has an id and I think id's will be needed. This suggests that the "names" of list elements shouldn't be used to generate tags. What I'm thinking is that the list members need to be character vectors with attached attributes. The "label" would be the string itself. A list inside the list would be understood to be a set of nodes attached to the preceding list (see below for an alternative). The (optional) attributes could then be used by the html-builder functions (tags...) to allow for customization. I'm thinking of having some keyword-driven attributes, like "open=TRUE" signaling the class="jstree-open" be added, "selected=TRUE", showing that this node be preselected, id="" would add the ID, maybe css="" and name="" will also be needed. These will dependent on the requirements of the jstree API. Using the idea above, I would see that the list would be formed something like this: s1 = "a" attributes(s1)=list(id="aa") s2 = "b" attributes(s2)=list(opened=TRUE) s3 = "b1" attributes(s3)=list(selected=TRUE,id="s3id") s4 = "b2" attributes(s2)=list(id="b2id") s5 = "c" tls = list(s1,s2,list(s3,s4),s5) The tree would look this when created: |- a |- b | |- b1 <<--selected | |- b2 |- c Another reasonable approach would have: tls = list(s1,list(s2,list(s3,s4)),s5) .... what would this mean, that s2 is a child of s1 with children s3 and s4, or is s2 at the same level of s1 with children s3 and s4. Comments? Sounds good, Patrick. Just to make sure it was clear -- multiple sessions (students) doing the quiz at the same time would likely not be an issue. The only problem would come if you were using Shiny Server Pro to run multiple processes of the quiz concurrently. In this case, the processes may be overwriting each other's updates. But if you have a single process and share the results data in the global process scope (http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html) you should be just fine.

Good luck!

you make your own fork of the repository and

So we took the most basic code and stripped everything but the server.R and ui.R codes, and got the app running on the server. As we keep adding things back in, the problem now is that when attempting to attach an Rmd file to one of the tabPanels in the ui, the entire App then returns: "Error: cannot open the connection". The code which is in a separate R file is this:

includeRmd <- function(path){
  contents <- paste(readLines(path, warn = FALSE), collapse = '\n')
  html <- knit2html(text = contents, fragment.only = TRUE, options = "", stylesheet = "www/empty.css")
  Encoding(html) <- 'UTF-8'
  HTML(html)
}

which the ui code has a source reference to.

We have gotten one of the Rmd files to attach to a tab panel by rendering a ui output in the server code like this:

output$homeui <-renderUI({
  list(
    includeCSS("homeui.css"),
      mainPanel(id = "intro",
      includeRmd("start.Rmd")
      )
    )
})

I was wondering if there was a solution to getting the includeRmd function to work on the ui page, or if there is another way of including Rmd files on a tabPanel. It appears to be the setup of the includeRmd, but  I am not sure exactly why since it works in the server ui rendering.

Certainly. Saving the output to different files would do the trick.

And the issue you describe is exactly the one that concerns me when running multiple processes. If you're only running one process, though, you can manage this with proper scoping. Here's some pseudo-code:

server.R
===========

myData <- getDatasetFromFTP()

shinyServer(function(input, output){
    observe({
        # Take a reactive dependency on the submit button so this observer fires on submit
        input$submit

        # Supplement the results with the current survey results.
        myData <<- rbind(myData, getSubmittedSurvey())

        # Persist the results to FTP
        saveDatasetToFTP(myData)
    })
})

This arrangement would keep the updated dataset in memory constantly, only reading from FTP once when the application is started. As long as only one of these processes runs at a time, you'll always have the authoritative/updated copy of your results in `myData`.

Clear as mud?

Jeff

My blind guess is that there is a problem of write permission. The R
process started by shiny server probably does not write permission to
the app directory. If that is the case, you can knit the report in a
temporary directory, e.g.

owd = setwd(tempdir())
library(knitr)
opts_knit$set(root.dir = owd)
# knit2html(....)
# and whatever you need to do after knitting
setwd(owd)

Regards,
Yihui

I've been trying to find a solution for this problem, but only stumbled into vague mentions.

The goal is to receive live data from a trading platform with IBrokers package, accumulate it, do computations with it periodically and as the user changes reactive inputs.
The package uses subscribe-callback mechanism to process new data. Once the data is requested, the function goes to a while(TRUE) loop and passes incoming messages to a callback function, where it can be written to a data frame, until stopped. Although it is not computationally intensive, it occupies the session.

Is it possible to update the data on a background and periodically do the calculations with it? I suspect it somehow involves multiple R sessions, since R is single threaded. I would appreciate any tips.

Not entirely the same question, but here's a related discussion <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/21282228/update-plot-within-observer-loop-in-shiny-application> and code <https://gist.github.com/trestletech/8608815> modeling one approach to a situation like this.

Not sure how well that will fit in your situation, though. I think you would be using this scheduler that works in chunks rather than a grand, blocking `while (TRUE)` call. There may be a simpler approach of just forcing Shiny to update its reactives periodically within your big loop, but I haven't explored that yet.

As far as I know, there's not an "official" best practice here. Would love to continue the discussion, though.

Jeff

To read a shapefile (user -> shiny), you have to use a multiple input, see there :

To write a shapefile (shiny -> user), the most convenient way is to create your shapefile files and then zip those, and return this zipped file to the user.

messages.subject: Re: How to keep data fresh (real-time data)
messages.subject_clean: How to keep data fresh (real-time data)
messages.body_plain:
I'm not quite clear on your method, but there may be room for improvement.

a.) You may have better luck with the table disappearing by using something like renderDataTable or just renderTable; I'm not familiar with gvisTable, so I'm not sure about that.
b.) How are you pulling the file in from Dropbox? If you're reading it in from disk (i.e. this server is registered as a Dropbox client and syncs all the files to disk constantly), then that looks great to me. If you're pulling it in from the web every few seconds, I'd recommend exploring alternatives (such as setting up the server as a Dropbox client, assuming you're hosting your own Shiny Server). One outstanding issue with R/Shiny is that HTTP requests are "blocking", meaning that the entire R process is tied up as long as the request is outstanding. So if the server is slow to respond, or if it takes a couple of seconds to download the data, the process will be unresponsive to other incoming requests (like users changing input and expecting new graphs to be generated) during that request. In your case, if you're doing this every 5 seconds, your users will likely notice that the app isn't too responsive.

On the other hand, if it's a non-interactive dashboard, that may be OK. As the data will just update every 5 seconds and doesn't need to be interactive.

Unfortunately, streaming of new data into Shiny isn't an area we've explored much. There are no technical reasons why it would be any more difficult than any other system, we just don't have any official "best practices" just yet.

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: Identify a polygon on a map based on user clicks
messages.subject_clean: Identify a polygon on a map based on user clicks
messages.body_plain:
I don't think there is any practical way to do what you want as long as you use ggplot2 to do your plotting.  Various people have suggested ways to use locator() and friends go from a mouse click in screen coordinates to user coordinates on a graph drawn with ggplot, but I've personally never gotten them to work.

In my experience, if you want to interact with a graph, you have to use base graphics and not ggplot.  Presumably the new gvis package fixes this - draws great graphics, with the same incremental process of building a plot and is highly interactive, but I haven't use it yet.

messages.subject: Re: Certificate error when using shinyapps::setAccountInfo() from behind a firewall
messages.subject_clean: Certificate error when using shinyapps::setAccountInfo() from behind a firewall
messages.body_plain:
I suspect your application name is invalid.  Application names must be at least 3 characters and cannot contain spaces. The application name defaults to the name of the directory where the application files are (which defaults to the current working directory).

If this is the case you can either a) rename your application directory

or b) manually specify an application name

deployApp(appName="some-name")

messages.subject: Re: shiny, ggplot2, and X11 on R 3.0.2
messages.subject_clean: shiny, ggplot2, and X11 on R 3.0.2
messages.body_plain:
Dear Daniel

I am no sure you did manage to solve this post... but just in case.

Most Linux "servers" do not have installed the graphical system X11 and most system admins will not be very kin on installing that (probably is difficult but I do not know if there is some other further issue like security reasons)

The function png in R/linux uses the X11 system and that is why you get the error.

Usually when I implement R code to be run in servers I use the function "bitmap" which does not depend up on the X11 and goes well. What I do not know is whether "bitmap" will go well with shiny...

I hope this helps.

David

On Thursday, February 27, 2014 1:33:12 AM UTC+1, Daniel Bowen wrote:
> Hello again. All libraries are up to date (as of a few hours ago).
>
> I recently had our sys admin - let's call him Joe - update R on an Amazon EC2 linux instance to v3.0.2, to deploy some new applications I've written that make use of dplyr. He was able to update R to v3.0.2, but, for whatever reason, he had to do it without X11. Displaying ggplot2 graphics within a shiny app returns an error where the graphic should be ("Error: X11 is not available"). Joe made it sound as if installing X11 on the Amazon EC2 linux instance is quite complicated. I have two questions:
>
> 1) is there a way to deploy ggplot2 + shiny without requiring X11? ... or,

messages.body_plain:
Veronica,

I am assuming you are using RStudio locally, and it is working for you there; right? RStudio searches your current directory for .Rprofile, and if that is not found then the .Rprofile file in your home directory is used. (As described in this document <http://www.rstudio.com/ide/docs/using/workspaces>).

Based on this document <http://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-patched/library/base/html/Startup.html>, when an R process starts, it should do the same thing (of course there are other environment settings that could affect this behavior).

In my own environment I see that if a .Rprofile file is in my current/application directory, then everything works fine, but not when it is in my home directory. So as a workaround, you could create the .Rprofile file in your application directory.

Best,
Fereshteh

hi, this is a common issue and i have worked out for times. my solution is  sample but a little time-comsuming:
first, you need know what your system version and try  to install the X11 lib (cause the next cairo will need some X11 libs: in centos  you can try
yum -y groupinstall "X Window System" "Desktop" "Fonts" "General Purpose Desktop"
see http://www.linuxquestions.org/questions/blog/gearge-611791/installing-the-graphical-window-system-x-org-x11-and-the-default-desktop-environment-on-centos-6-4098/)
then, install cairo-devel and recompile your R from source code with ./configure --with-x=no
to check wether the steps above  is ok, open your R  and type capabilities()
you may see

   jpeg       png            tiff           tcltk        X11       aqua         http/ftp s ockets      libxml     fifo   cledit
  TRUE     TRUE     TRUE     TRUE       FALSE     TRUE     TRUE     TRUE     TRUE     TRUE
   iconv        NLS       profmem    cairo
    TRUE     TRUE     TRUE     TRUE
please note that the cairo must be true, and if not ,there must be some thing wrong in your packages'installlation(PS: in your R, cairo package must be also installed)
if you see the output like i mentioned above , it means you can generated common images now.
 PS : this is non of shiny's bussiness.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe

I'm trying to write a little app that allows users to upload and process some CSVs of brand by statement for correspondence map.

I'm noticing some error--  I've attached here a sample csv and will paste some code in below for my file upload. Any thoughts, if time permits, would be greatly appreciated.

ui.r

library ("FactoMineR")
library ("shiny")
  shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
    headerPanel("File input test"),
    sidebarPanel(
      fileInput("df", "File data", multiple=TRUE)
    ),

       mainPanel( # all of the output elements go in here
        h3("This is Correspondance Map"),

        plotOutput("caPlot")
       )
  ))

server.r

library (FactoMineR)
library (shiny)
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$caPlot <- renderPlot({
    inFile <- input$df

    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)
    dataset<-read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=T, stringsAsFactors =F)

    ca2 = CA(dataset, graph = FALSE)
          plot(ca2)

    })
  })

Abhishek

On Wednesday, 6 March 2013 03:50:00 UTC+5:30, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> Many of you have been waiting patiently for file upload improvements in Shiny, especially fixing file uploads on Shiny Server. We're pretty close now, but it involved writing a whole lot of new code so I'd like to see some beta testing before we release to CRAN.
>
> Please help us beta test by following the upgrade instructions at the end of this message.
>
> Features:
> Now works with Shiny Server! (glimmer.rstudio.com <http://glimmer.rstudio.com> is already upgraded)
> Local uploads are also much faster and more robust
> Progress is displayed during upload
> Limitations:
> (Still) not compatible with IE9 and earlier
> Uploads cannot be canceled (other than reloading the page)
> Note:
> By default, Shiny limits file upload requests to 5MB; anything larger will be rejected. You can change this limit using option(shiny.maxRequestSize = x), where x is the size in bytes; a size of -1 means any size is allowed.
> ----
>
> Instructions for upgrading a Shiny Server install:
>
> Run these commands from the shell:
>
> sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('shiny', repos=c(RStudio='http://rstudio.org/_packages', CRAN='http://cran.rstudio.com'))\""
>
> sudo npm install -g https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/tarball/httpuv
>
> Then restart Shiny Server. If you're using Upstart, the command is sudo restart shiny-server
>
>
> Instructions for upgrading a non-server Shiny install:
>
> Run this command from the R console:
>
> install.packages('shiny', repos=c(RStudio='http://rstudio.org/_packages', CRAN='http://cran.rstudio.com'))
>
> Then restart your R session.
>

messages.subject: Re: what happens when a user 'drops' a Shiny app in progress?
messages.subject_clean: what happens when a user 'drops' a Shiny app in progress?
messages.body_plain:
The answers are actually a little complicated.

If a user closes a window, then generally the current calculations executing on behalf of the user need to complete--we don't have a way to detect and abort the current calculations. The exception is if the useR leaving means there is nobody using that particular R process; then shiny server will wait a few seconds then ask the whole process to shut down.

There's no "never mind" button, no. I've never thought about it but that's interesting, I wonder whether it's even possible given how reactive programming works to interrupt a set of calculations and still have the world be in a consistent state. I'll think about it...

messages.subject: Re: Is is possible to build UI objects using for loops in the shiny ui.R?
messages.subject_clean: Is is possible to build UI objects using for loops in the shiny ui.R?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

this is very well possible. Let's say you want to construct a set of 10 radio button inputs in an automatic way. For this you can use renderUI, uiOutput and reactiveValuesToList :
Furthermore, it is useful to realize renderUI can take a list as well.

In server.r you would have something like this:

output$Dynamic <- renderUI({
      L <- vector("list",10)
      for(i in 1:10){
            LL[[i]] <- list(radioButtons(inputId = paste0("mVariable",i), label = paste0("mVariable",i), choices = c("A","B","C")))
      }
})

in ui.R you call:

uiOutput("Dynamic")

in turn, in server.r you can retrieve the values for the generated inputs by:

isolate(unlist(reactiveValuesToList(input)[paste0("mVariable",1:10)]))

the isolate function is used to prevent taken a dependency on all input elements, which can make your app very slow

hope this helps!

kind regards, Herman

Hi everyone,
I am a new shiny user and I totally love it, I have a question that I hope is not too obvious that I hope someone can help shed some light on.

I have several tabPanels in my app and one of them contains a ggvis interactive plot.  Loading this plot dramatically slows the loading of all the other tabPanels after the settings are changed. To address this, I would like to be able to only run the interactive plot when the user is on the interactive plot page/ clicks a submit button or similar.

Reading the help docs, I found isolate (http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/isolation.html) might be what I want, but I am having a hard time adapting that to within the observe_ggvis call. Is there something obvious that I am missing, is there a different way I should be observing the ggvis plot to allow this functionality?

thanks in advance,
-brandi

for the sake of example, a snippet of my ui and sever scripts are below.  Hopefully
ui.R:
tabsetPanel(
# static plot
  tabPanel("static_plot",
                plotOutput("plot1")
               ),

# interactive plot
 tabPanel("interactive_plot",
               ggvis_output(plot_id="my_plot")
              ),

# data output
tabPanel("data",
             tableOutput("table1")
             )
)

server.R
# fxns to process data according to user inputs...

output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
       print(<output from ggplot2 static plot>)
       )}

observe_ggvis(<gv returned from ggvis fxn not shown>, "myplot", session)

output$table1 <- renderTable({
       <df returned from fxns not shown>
        })

messages.subject: Re: Gow to set my shinyApp url without port number?
messages.subject_clean: Gow to set my shinyApp url without port number?
messages.body_plain:
Aurelien is correct. If your port 80 is already occupied, you won't be able to run Shiny Server on port 80 which means your users will need to specify a port number.

The one exception would be if you're willing to setup an HTTP proxy like Apache or nginx. One of those systems could selectively forward certain traffic from port 80 (for instance, traffic prefaced with "/shiny") to Shiny Server.

Jeff

messages.subject: why "subscript out of bounds" error in Shiny but not R?
messages.subject_clean: why "subscript out of bounds" error in Shiny but not R?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

We have a confounding issue in the Shiny app that we are developing. As the subject indicates, we get an "error: subscript out of bounds" message upon running the app. However, when we isolate the offending code and run it on its own in RStudio, there is no error.

Please see the instructions below and the attached .R files for details. We are using Shiny version 0.8.0 and RStudio 0.98.501.

Is this a Shiny bug, or are we missing something?

Thanks,
Byran Smucker

----

To run the app, place ui.R and server.R (both attached) in a folder and run

library(shiny)
runApp("<folder path>")

It should produce a user interface with a button on the left, but on the right you will see "error: subscript out of bounds".

However, if just run the following three lines of code (lines 57-59 in server.R)

  show=data.frame(ps=c(4,-1,0,1),ns=c(0,1,0,0),ts=c(45842,15653,28535,21656))
  best.fit1=regsubsets(ts~ps+ns,data=show,nvmax=1)
  pred1=predict.regsubsets(best.fit1,show,id=1)  # line that offends Shiny

in RStudio (need to include the function "predict.regsubsets" - given at the beginning of server.R), then there are no errors.

messages.subject_clean: Change the reactivity ordering in a Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi Folks,

I have used Rstudio Shiny package to develop a disease monitoring system. This system includes 55 diseases and three trigonometric models are used to monitor them. Since the behavior of each disease is different, the default delected model for each disease is different but known. e.g. "First order Trig model"' is better for Ecoli O157, "Second order" is better for Rocky Mountatin Fever, etc. However, the user can change the model to evaluate other models on a single disease type.

Since the codes for the system are too lengthy, i wrote a part of my ui.R and server. R codes:

------------------------------------------------------------------------
ui.R
selectInput("disease", "Choose the disease:", choices=c( "Anaplasma Phagocytophilum", ...) ),
sliderInput( "L" , label="Factor for Control Limits",  min=2 , max=6 , value=3 , step=0.2 , animate=T) ,
...
uiOutput("degree"),
....
showOutput("myPlot", "highcharts")
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
server.R

  output$degree <- renderUI({

     if (input$disease %in% degreeZero) {
      selectInput("degree0", " Choose  trigonometric
    regression model?" , choices=c("Zero Order Model", "First Order Model","Second Order Model"), selected="Zero Order Model")
    }

    else if (input$disease %in% degreeOne) {
        selectInput("degree1", " Choose  trigonometric
    regression model?" , choices=c("Zero Order Model", "First Order Model","Second Order Model"), selected="First Order Model")
      }

    else {
        selectInput("degree2", " Choose  trigonometric
    regression model?" , choices=c("Zero Order Model", "First Order Model","Second Order Model"), selected="Second Order Model")
      }

  })

  output$myPlot <- renderChart2(
{
essentially employs the inputs and measure the control limits and spit out the Control Charts
}

-----------------------------------------------------------

and My Question is: when I change the disease names, The model computes control limits using the previous model and after a short bit of time it recognizes that the model type is also updated. I guess the reason is because of the reactivity order. I mean the package first updates the disease, then run the R codes and spit out outputs. Since one of the outputs is model type (uiOutput("degree") change, it reruns the R codes and show the new control chart.

Is there anyway in R shiny to ractive a special output before running R codes?

Thank you in advance,
Ehsan
